_note: Bortle classes: Frosty Drew and K.D. Dubuque are published values; Myles Standish, Race Point, Heins Farm, and Kancamagus are light-pollution map estimates (no published on-site measurements found as of 2026-09-16). The 53 nationwide DarkSky-certified sites added 2026-09-16 use published Bortle values where available (Cherry Springs, South Llano River) and light-pollution map estimates otherwise — each entry says which. Treat all map estimates as planning guides, not on-site measurements. Drive times on the New England entries are typical ranges.
_source: Sky & Telescope — Tony Flanders skyglow measurements (Boston area, for Medford proxy)
Frederick William House New England stargazing guide (outer-Cape Bortle 3–4)
frostydrew.org; mass.gov; The Last Green Valley (site access details)
DarkSky International (darksky.org) Dark Sky Places listings and designation announcements
U.S. National Park Service, U.S. Forest Service, and state park agency pages (site access and dark-sky programs)
Texas Parks and Wildlife and Pennsylvania DCNR (published Bortle values for South Llano River and Cherry Springs)

sites.access: Free public stargazing every Friday night, year-round (weather permitting). Red-light-only campus: no white lights dusk–dawn.
sites.address: Ninigret Park, 62 Park Lane, Charlestown, RI 02813
sites.highlights: Guided observing with large telescopes; Milky Way plainly visible; special events for meteor showers and eclipses.
sites.name: Frosty Drew Observatory
sites.bortle_source: Frosty Drew's own observing log: ~2.5 overhead, ~4.5 toward the Providence/Westerly horizons (NELM ~6.25)

sites.access: Night access via seasonal campgrounds (400+ sites; advance reservations). Day-use areas close at dusk.
sites.highlights: Big dark pine-barrens forest close to Boston; combine observing with an overnight camp.
sites.name: Myles Standish State Forest
sites.bortle_source: Light-pollution map estimate — no published on-site measurement found

sites.access: Seashore beaches, parking, and trails open 6 AM–midnight — fine for evening observing, not an all-night site. Seasonal beach fees may apply.
sites.highlights: Open ocean horizons in nearly every direction at the tip of the Cape; classic meteor-shower spot.
sites.name: Cape Cod National Seashore — Race Point
sites.bortle_source: Map estimate; outer-Cape beaches described as Bortle 3–4 in a local guide — no site-specific measurement found

sites.access: Free parking at the trailhead. Organized night events have been held here; confirm after-dark access before visiting.
sites.highlights: Big open field shielded from headlights, in the dark-sky corridor of the Last Green Valley.
sites.name: Heins Farm Conservation Area (Sturbridge Trails)
sites.bortle_source: Light-pollution map estimate — no published on-site measurement found

sites.access: Public highway through White Mountain National Forest; overlook pullouts accessible at night. A day-use pass may be required for parking areas.
sites.highlights: Mountain pass at 2,855 ft with wide scenic overlooks (e.g., Pemigewasset Overlook); genuinely dark northern skies.
sites.name: Kancamagus Highway — Pemigewasset Overlook
sites.bortle_source: Light-pollution map estimate — no published on-site measurement found

sites.access: mass.gov lists hours as sunrise–sunset; night access is via wilderness camping only. Remote area — plan accordingly.
sites.address: 466 W. Hawley Road, Plainfield, MA 01070 (entrance on MA-8A, Hawley)
sites.highlights: One of the darkest accessible spots in Massachusetts; wilderness camping under the Milky Way.
sites.name: Kenneth Dubuque Memorial State Forest
sites.bortle_source: Published rating on the go-astronomy.com dark-sky directory

sites.access: Park roads are open around the clock; campgrounds and backcountry roads need planning, and carry plenty of water.
sites.highlights: The largest International Dark Sky Park in the U.S., with some of the darkest skies in the country. Furnace Creek and Dante's View are favorite stargazing spots.
sites.name: Death Valley National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Open 24/7; reserve campgrounds well ahead in peak season.
sites.highlights: Famous for Joshua trees silhouetted against the Milky Way, with regular ranger-led night-sky programs. Winter brings the clearest skies.
sites.name: Joshua Tree National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Visitor center in Borrego Springs; many dirt roads are fine for regular cars.
sites.highlights: California's largest state park surrounds Borrego Springs, itself a Dark Sky Community. Desert wildflowers are a spring bonus.
sites.name: Anza-Borrego Desert State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: The main park road is usually open late May to October; snow closes it in winter.
sites.highlights: A quieter national park with dark skies and summer star parties. Milky Way season runs June through September.
sites.name: Lassen Volcanic National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: The Wheeler Peak scenic drive climbs 12 miles; check road status in winter.
sites.highlights: One of the least-visited national parks, home to ancient bristlecone pines and Lehman Caves. The astronomy festival is each September.
sites.name: Great Basin National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: High-clearance vehicle recommended on County Road 8A; primitive Leave No Trace camping only; check conditions with the BLM first.
sites.highlights: A 101,000-acre International Dark Sky Sanctuary and one of the darkest places in the lower 48. No campgrounds or services — a true expedition.
sites.name: Massacre Rim Wilderness Study Area
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Open 24/7 year-round; the main road can close in heavy snow.
sites.highlights: Bryce's hoodoos glow under some of the darkest skies of any national park, with over 100 astronomy programs a year. The Astronomy Festival is in June.
sites.name: Bryce Canyon National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Timed-entry reservations required in peak season; the park is open 24 hours.
sites.highlights: More than 2,000 natural stone arches under dark desert skies, an easy drive from Moab.
sites.name: Arches National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: No food or water in the park — fill up in Moab before heading in.
sites.highlights: Vast canyon country with some of Utah's darkest accessible skies. Island in the Sky is the easiest district to reach.
sites.name: Canyonlands National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Open 24/7; the scenic drive is paved but side roads can be rough.
sites.highlights: A remote park of red-rock cliffs and orchards with Gold-tier dark skies and a growing astronomy program.
sites.name: Capitol Reef National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Shuttle required in Zion Canyon most of the year; Kolob Terrace Road is a quieter night-sky alternative.
sites.highlights: Towering canyon walls block nearby town lights, giving surprisingly dark skies for such a popular park.
sites.name: Zion National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: The 9-mile Bridge View Drive loop is open day and night.
sites.highlights: The world's first International Dark Sky Park (2006), named for three massive natural bridges. Among the darkest skies reachable by paved road.
sites.name: Natural Bridges National Monument
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Day-use fee; the park stays open for night-sky viewing after the visitor center closes.
sites.highlights: A mesa-top park with a 2,000-foot overlook of the Colorado River, a short drive from Moab. Popular for Milky Way photography.
sites.name: Dead Horse Point State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Day-use fee; camping available in the park.
sites.highlights: A valley of mushroom-shaped rock 'goblins' that make surreal foregrounds for night photography. Small and easy to explore after dark.
sites.name: Goblin Valley State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Day-use fee; the island closes at night except for registered campers and special star parties.
sites.highlights: Utah's largest island in the Great Salt Lake, with bison herds and dark skies a short drive from Salt Lake City.
sites.name: Antelope Island State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Day-use fee; campground on site.
sites.highlights: A small park of colorful spires and chimneys, designated a Dark Sky Park in 2021. Quieter and darker than nearby Bryce Canyon.
sites.name: Kodachrome Basin State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: The Colorado-side entrance near Dinosaur has the main visitor center; backcountry roads need high clearance.
sites.highlights: A park spanning Utah and Colorado, famous for its dinosaur quarry and dark river-canyon skies. Designated a Dark Sky Park in 2019.
sites.name: Dinosaur National Monument
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: South Rim road open roughly April to November; the North Rim is gravel and more remote.
sites.highlights: A steep, narrow canyon whose depth swallows stray light, making for very dark skies. The Astronomy Festival is in September.
sites.name: Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Open 24/7; the main dune field is a short walk from the parking area.
sites.highlights: The tallest dunes in North America against the Sangre de Cristo Mountains — and a designated Dark Sky Park.
sites.name: Great Sand Dunes National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Open during posted hours; check the schedule for evening programs.
sites.highlights: A fossil-bed monument of giant petrified redwoods with dark skies an hour from Colorado Springs. Night-sky programs run in summer.
sites.name: Florissant Fossil Beds National Monument
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: The 20-mile access road is rough dirt — allow extra time and check conditions.
sites.highlights: An ancient Puebloan great-house complex aligned with the sun and moon, now a Gold-tier Dark Sky Park. Ranger night-sky programs run spring through fall.
sites.name: Chaco Culture National Historical Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Free, first-come, first-served; vault toilets, no water; 8 miles north of Alma off US-180.
sites.highlights: North America's first International Dark Sky Sanctuary (2016): a small free campground in the Gila National Forest with a 360-degree horizon and telescope pads.
sites.name: Cosmic Campground
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: NM-4 pullouts open 24/7; main visitor areas keep posted hours.
sites.highlights: A massive volcanic crater with wide-open grassland skies, designated in 2021. The Valle Grande pullouts on NM-4 are open for stargazing around the clock.
sites.name: Valles Caldera National Preserve
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Day-use fee; campground on site.
sites.highlights: A small northeastern New Mexico park known for dinosaur footprints and monthly star parties with a 14-inch telescope. Gold-tier dark skies.
sites.name: Clayton Lake State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: The park closes overnight except for backcountry campers with a permit.
sites.highlights: Painted Desert badlands and 200-million-year-old fossil trees under dark high-desert skies. Designated a Dark Sky Park in 2019.
sites.name: Petrified Forest National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Open 24/7 year-round; the North Rim closes in winter.
sites.highlights: One of the seven natural wonders, certified as a Dark Sky Park, with star parties each June. The South Rim is easiest to reach; the North Rim is darker.
sites.name: Grand Canyon National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Cave tours by reservation; the park opens late for scheduled night programs.
sites.highlights: A living cave system in the Whetstone Mountains foothills with a Dark Sky Park above ground. Evening star programs run in season.
sites.name: Kartchner Caverns State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Day-use fee; check the schedule for evening star-party events.
sites.highlights: A small park north of Tucson dedicated to environmental education, with skies protected by local lighting codes. Regular star parties.
sites.name: Oracle State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Very remote — gas up before entering; lodging books out months ahead.
sites.highlights: Texas's great wilderness park, a Gold-tier Dark Sky Park with some of the darkest skies in North America. Chisos Basin and Rio Grande Village are favorite spots.
sites.name: Big Bend National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Day-use fee; reserve McDonald Observatory star-party tickets separately.
sites.highlights: High-country skies in the Davis Mountains, a short drive from McDonald Observatory's famous star parties. The park itself is a Dark Sky Park.
sites.name: Davis Mountains State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Day passes sell out — reserve ahead; the park closes at night except for campers.
sites.highlights: A giant pink-granite dome in the Hill Country with dark skies an hour from Austin and San Antonio.
sites.name: Enchanted Rock State Natural Area
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Day-use fee; campground on site.
sites.highlights: A Hill Country river park designated in 2017. A good first dark-sky trip from central Texas.
sites.name: South Llano River State Park
sites.bortle_source: Texas Parks and Wildlife Department (published)

sites.access: The astronomy field is open 24/7 for registered overnight observers; white light is banned after dark.
sites.address: Cherry Springs State Park, Coudersport, PA 16915
sites.highlights: Pennsylvania's legendary astronomy park with a dedicated overnight observing field and some of the darkest skies in the East.
sites.name: Cherry Springs State Park
sites.bortle_source: Pennsylvania DCNR (published)

sites.access: Cabins and campgrounds on site; the lake area has open sky views.
sites.highlights: West Virginia's largest state park, designated in 2021 along with neighboring Calvin Price State Forest. One of the darkest spots in the mid-Atlantic.
sites.name: Watoga State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Day-use fee; campground and cabins on site.
sites.highlights: A quiet park on the Virginia–North Carolina line, one of the first Dark Sky Parks on the East Coast.
sites.name: Staunton River State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Day-use fee; limited services — bring everything you need and check road conditions after rain.
sites.highlights: Florida's first Dark Sky Park: a vast dry prairie with big open horizons, great for Milky Way panoramas.
sites.name: Kissimmee Prairie Preserve State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Day-use fee; cabins and campground; boat tours run by day.
sites.highlights: A park inside the Okefenokee Swamp, certified as a Dark Sky Park. Alligators by day, Milky Way by night.
sites.name: Stephen C. Foster State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Day-use fee; campground and cabins; the viewing field is open after dark.
sites.highlights: A Tennessee park built by the Civilian Conservation Corps, with dark skies and a dedicated viewing field. Hosts an annual star party.
sites.name: Pickett CCC Memorial State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Free; canoe launches double as stargazing spots; no services after dark.
sites.highlights: America's first national river, with dark skies along its bluffs and gravel bars. Tyler Bend and Steel Creek are good night-sky spots.
sites.name: Buffalo National River
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Day-use fee; lodge, cabins, and campground on site.
sites.highlights: An Arkansas mountaintop park with overlooks of the Arkansas River Valley and certified dark skies.
sites.name: Petit Jean State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Nebraska park permit required; the star party is in late July/early August.
sites.highlights: A Sandhills reservoir famous among astronomers as home of the annual Nebraska Star Party. Designated a Dark Sky Park in 2022.
sites.name: Merritt Reservoir State Recreation Area
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Open 24/7; the South Unit near Medora is easiest to reach.
sites.highlights: Badlands wilderness in North Dakota with certified dark skies and a growing night-sky program. Bison may wander past your telescope.
sites.name: Theodore Roosevelt National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Day-use fee; drive-in and backpack campsites; the Europe Bay lot is a good viewing spot.
sites.highlights: Wisconsin's only wilderness-designated state park, on the tip of Door County with dark skies over Lake Michigan. Designated in 2017.
sites.name: Newport State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Open 24/7; the Waterfront Event Center hosts night programs.
sites.highlights: A 600-acre county-run Dark Sky Park on the Straits of Mackinac with guest programs. One of the best aurora-watching spots in the Lower 48.
sites.name: Headlands International Dark Sky Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Centered on the Keweenaw Mountain Lodge in Copper Harbor; trails open to the public.
sites.highlights: Michigan's Keweenaw Peninsula dark-sky park, centered on the Mountain Lodge, with some of the darkest skies in the Midwest and regular aurora displays.
sites.name: Keweenaw Dark Sky Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Loop road open roughly May to November; campground is first-come, first-served.
sites.highlights: A lava-field landscape that feels like another planet, designated a Dark Sky Park in 2019. Summer star parties on the loop road.
sites.name: Craters of the Moon National Monument
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Use Ketchum or Stanley as a base; the Salmon River pullouts have wide-open skies.
sites.highlights: America's first International Dark Sky Reserve (2017), covering the Sun Valley, Ketchum, and Stanley area — a whole valley committed to dark skies.
sites.name: Central Idaho Dark Sky Reserve
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Going-to-the-Sun Road needs a vehicle reservation in summer; many areas close with snow.
sites.highlights: Waterton-Glacier became the world's first cross-border Dark Sky Park, fully certified in 2021. Logan Pass and St. Mary are favorite night spots.
sites.name: Glacier National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Permit required May–September; entry points near Ely; no motors allowed.
sites.highlights: A million-acre wilderness of lakes and forest, designated an International Dark Sky Sanctuary in 2020. Paddle in, camp, and watch the sky from your canoe.
sites.name: Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Visitor centers at Rainy Lake and Kabetogama; boat tours and houseboat rentals available.
sites.highlights: Minnesota's water-based national park, certified as a Dark Sky Park in 2020. Unlike the Boundary Waters, motorboats are allowed, so it's easier to visit.
sites.name: Voyageurs National Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Day-use fee; campgrounds on both sides of the reservoir.
sites.highlights: Central Oregon's Dark Sky Park on a high-desert reservoir, designated in 2021. An easy dark-sky trip from Bend.
sites.name: Prineville Reservoir State Park
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Use Lakeview as a base; services are sparse across the sanctuary — carry extra fuel and water.
sites.highlights: A 2.5-million-acre International Dark Sky Sanctuary (2024) covering much of Lake County — the largest dark-sky sanctuary in the world. Genuinely remote high desert.
sites.name: Oregon Outback International Dark Sky Sanctuary
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement

sites.access: Gravel roads off ME-11; no visitor center — plan it like a backcountry trip.
sites.highlights: An 87,500-acre national monument east of Baxter State Park, designated an International Dark Sky Sanctuary in 2020. Dark skies and a good shot at the northern lights.
sites.name: Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument
sites.bortle_source: Estimate from light-pollution maps; not an on-site measurement
